mcqs.question: Which of the following best describes the conjunction (AND) of two statements P and Q?

options.A: It is true only when both P and Q are true.
options.B: It is true when either P or Q is true.
options.C: It is true when P is true and Q is false.
options.D: It is true only when both P and Q are false.

mcqs.answer: It is true only when both P and Q are true.
mcqs.explanation: The conjunction P ∧ Q is true only in the case where both component statements are true; in all other cases (one false or both false) the conjunction is false. Option B describes disjunction, C and D are incorrect definitions.

mcqs.question: The disjunction (OR) of statements P and Q is false only when:

options.A: Both P and Q are true.
options.B: At least one of P or Q is true.
options.C: Both P and Q are false.
options.D: Exactly one of P or Q is true.

mcqs.answer: Both P and Q are false.
mcqs.explanation: For the inclusive OR (P ∨ Q), the compound statement is true if at least one component is true. It becomes false only when both components are false. Hence option C is correct; the other options describe true conditions.

mcqs.question: In the implication "If P then Q", what is the truth value when P is false and Q is true?
mcqs.explanation: An implication P → Q is considered true whenever the antecedent P is false, regardless of the truth value of Q. This is sometimes called a vacuous truth. Therefore the correct answer is True. Option B would be correct only when P is true and Q is false.

mcqs.question: Let P be "It is raining" and Q be "The ground is wet". Which of the following statements correctly represents the biconditional relationship between P and Q?

options.A: If it is raining then the ground is wet.
options.B: The ground is wet if and only if it is raining.
options.C: It is raining or the ground is wet.
options.D: It is not raining and the ground is not wet.

mcqs.answer: The ground is wet if and only if it is raining.
mcqs.explanation: A biconditional (P ↔ Q) asserts that P and Q have the same truth value: both true or both false. It is expressed as "P if and only if Q". Option B captures this meaning. Option A is a simple implication, C is a disjunction, and D is a conjunction of negations, none of which convey the biconditional.

mcqs.question: Consider the compound statement P ∧ (Q ∨ R). What is its truth value when P is true, Q is false, and R is true?
mcqs.explanation: First evaluate the inner disjunction: Q ∨ R = false ∨ true = true. Then the whole expression becomes P ∧ true = true ∧ true = true. Hence the compound statement is true. Options B, C, and D are incorrect.

mcqs.question: A student passes Mathematics and passes Physics. Which of the following statements about the conjunction is correct if the student passes Mathematics but fails Physics?
mcqs.explanation: A conjunction requires both component statements to be true. Since the student fails Physics, the second component is false, making the whole conjunction false. Option A contradicts the definition, C is not applicable, and D is factually wrong.

mcqs.question: A common misconception is that "P OR Q" is true only when exactly one of P or Q is true. Which statement correctly describes the truth condition for the logical OR?

options.A: True only when exactly one of P or Q is true.
options.B: True when at least one of P or Q is true.
options.C: True only when both P and Q are true.
options.D: True only when both P and Q are false.

mcqs.answer: True when at least one of P or Q is true.
mcqs.explanation: The inclusive OR (∨) is true if either or both component statements are true. It is false only when both are false. Option A describes the exclusive OR, which is not the standard logical OR used in mathematical reasoning.

mcqs.question: For the implication "If it is snowing then the temperature is below 0°C", which of the following situations makes the implication false?

options.A: It is snowing and the temperature is below 0°C.
options.B: It is not snowing and the temperature is above 0°C.
options.C: It is snowing and the temperature is above 0°C.
options.D: It is not snowing and the temperature is below 0°C.

mcqs.answer: It is snowing and the temperature is above 0°C.
mcqs.explanation: An implication P → Q is false only when the antecedent P is true and the consequent Q is false. Here, P = "it is snowing" and Q = "temperature is below 0°C". The only case that violates the implication is when it is snowing (P true) but the temperature is not below 0°C (Q false), which is option C. All other options satisfy the implication.
